Debt Settlement | Enrollment Process (SOP)

Level Debt backend · Forth platform · v1.0
Start here

What this SOP covers

This is the standard process for enrolling a client into a Level Debt settlement program through Forth, from the first data capture on the call through to the compliance handoff. It reflects the current process, including the required Basic Legal Plan update.

Policy update in effect Every Level Debt enrollment now includes a Basic Legal Plan ($19.99) built into the program payment, so clients who are not also taking Level Coaching are covered by legal protection. This changes which Base Plan and document package you select during enrollment — details are in the Enrollment Process and Quick Reference tabs.

Default assumption for this SOP

Unless a client is explicitly being offered Level Coaching, treat every enrollment as Level Debt only, no coaching. That means: original-plus-Legal-1.0 base plan, the LP document package, and the standard compliance script. A separate SOP will cover the Level Coaching add-on path in more detail; this version includes the coaching steps for reference but assumes it is the exception, not the default.

What qualifies for the program

Acceptable debt

  • Unsecured credit cards & loans
  • Payday & tribal loans
  • Repossessions, medical & back rent (<50% of total debt)
  • Private student loans (≤25% of total, client no longer enrolled)
  • Non-operational or unprofitable business debt
  • Discover (≤60% of total — see Discover rule)

Not acceptable

  • Federal / Navient student loans, SBA loans
  • Timeshares, IRS/taxes, alimony/child support
  • Casino debt, cash call, overdraft accounts
  • Debts from employers
  • Private student loans for CA residents
  • Discover private student loans
500+Min. creditor score
$7,000Min. total enrolled debt
$200Min. per account ($1 if already in collections)
$250Min. positive monthly budget
1 paymentMade on the debt already

How debt settlement programs work

There are two paths through the program, depending on whether the client funds settlements by saving monthly or accelerates with a loan.

Traditional · 22–28 months

Enrollment → Monthly payments into an FDIC-insured account → Debt ages to improve settlement leverage → Negotiators settle accounts → Debt free

Loan / Accelerated · 6–12 months

Enrollment → Monthly payments → 6 consecutive payments qualifies the client to apply for a loan → Negotiators settle accounts → Loan funded, debt free

Who supports the client after enrollment

Account Specialist (AS)

Assigned to every client after compliance. Meets bi-weekly until the first settlement, then monthly through the rest of the program. Main point of contact for questions.

Financial Success Coach (FSC)

Only for clients with Level Coaching. Certified coach providing monthly one-on-one support; an intro call is scheduled immediately after enrollment.

Level Coaching — only if offering coaching

Default for this SOP: skip this step. Only complete it if the client is explicitly being enrolled in Level Coaching alongside debt settlement.

  • From the Edit Contact dropdown, select the Level Benefits form.
  • Fields: Benefit Type, Initial Investment Amount ($299 unless an exception is approved — can be split over multiple pays), Initial Investment Date (within 30 days of enrollment), card info if needed, Monthly ACH Benefit ($59/$49/$39/$29), and Monthly ACH Benefit Date (within 30 days of the initial investment).
  • If coaching is not being offered, set Benefit Type to "No Benefits" and move on.
Decision point · program setup

Enrollment Plan & Base Plan Selection

Open the Enrollment tab. Select the Plan Account — Level Debt in green states, Pinnacle Legal in red states (refer to the state list).

Debt Settlement Enrollment Plan — Select a Base Plan & Program Length
Legal fee crossover — read before selecting a Base Plan
  • No Level Coaching → select "Debt Settlement Enrollment + Legal 1.0" (or the Upper Management version for exception term lengths). This adds the $19.99 legal fee, shown as its own line in the Payment Schedule.
  • With Level Coaching → select the original "Debt Settlement Enrollment" base plan (no "+ Legal"). Coaching already includes legal protection, so adding Legal 1.0 here would double-charge the client.

Discover accounts Discover is the most litigious creditor and settles highest on average (~70%). Its enrolled balance cannot exceed 60% of total enrolled debt. To size the draft: (Discover balance × 70%) ÷ 24 — e.g. $15,600 Discover debt → the client's payment should be at or above ~$455/mo.

Choose a Program Length to see the updated Total Payment, and check/uncheck accounts on the Debts list to see how enrolling different debts changes it. Then select Pay Frequency (Monthly, Semi-Monthly, or Bi-Weekly) — first payment should land within 5–10 business days. Save the Enrollment Plan and click back into the client's name.

System action

Submit & Send Compliance Email

Why this step exists Funding Tier runs its own secure Forth instance to protect our leads and data. Level Debt's backend — debt negotiators, the law firm, and client services — does not have direct, immediate access to our Forth account. The compliance email is how we bridge that gap: it's a heads-up to Level Debt's compliance department that says, in effect, "we're submitting this file to you, and here are its exact details." Those details dynamically populate the standard script their compliance team reads back to the client during their own Quality Control (QC) call. That QC call is how Level Debt independently confirms the details of the enrollment directly with the client we're submitting — so getting this email right matters as much as the submission itself.

Once documents are signed: Enrollment tab → Edit Enrollment → Submit File. This webhooks the client into the system — changes made after submitting won't be recorded.

Then, from the client's Emails tab, send the compliance email. Update the "To" field to contracts@level-debt.com — it defaults to the client, so double-check before sending.

Send An Email — To field and template picker

Client-facing · QC

Compliance Call

Warm transfer the client to the dedicated compliance line. Once that call is complete, the enrollment is done.

What happens right after enrollment Every client is assigned a dedicated Account Specialist (AS), who becomes their main point of contact — meeting bi-weekly until the first settlement, then monthly for the rest of the program. If the client also took Level Coaching, they're additionally paired with a Financial Success Coach (FSC) for monthly one-on-one support, with an intro call scheduled immediately after enrollment.
Confirmed from the live system There isn't yet a separate "LP"-specific compliance template — the standard Level/Pinnacle Compliance Script templates (NO Benefits / and Benefits) are what's currently used regardless of the legal fee. Flag with your team lead if that should change once the LP rollout is complete everywhere.

Keeping the call moving toward enrollment

The most common place calls stall is between the budget and the enrollment plan — once you've confirmed a client's debts qualify and their cash flow supports a payment, move directly into building the Enrollment Plan while you're still talking, rather than summarizing and coming back to it later. Walking through Program Length and watching the Total Payment update live with the client keeps the conversation concrete and moving forward instead of turning into a callback.

Needs input from your team This SOP doesn't yet include your compliance-approved talking points for the discovery, objection-handling, or close portions of the call, or the specific structure of the Welcome Call (what it covers, when it happens relative to enrollment, and who runs it). Send over your current call script or Welcome Call checklist and I'll build those out as a proper walkthrough in this tab — I didn't want to invent debt-settlement sales language that hasn't been compliance-reviewed.
Step 3

Filling out the Budget Analysis

Getting an accurate budget is what determines whether a client can actually sustain a program payment.

Filling Out the Budget AnalysisScreen recording
Cash Flow updates live as each income & expense line is filled in
Cash Flow must be $250 or more to qualify
  • Open the Budget Analysis tab from the client's record.
  • Enter all monthly income sources on the left, and all monthly expenses on the right.
  • If an expense is shared with someone else, only include the portion the client is responsible for.
  • The top of the screen auto-calculates Total Net Income, Total Expenses, Expense %, Cash Flow, and Total Assets as you go.
  • Cash Flow must be at least $250 for the client to qualify.
  • Click Save Budget at the top before leaving the screen — unsaved data is lost.
  • Click the client's name to return to the main profile.
Step 2 detail

Understanding the credit report

A quick reference for reading what comes back after you pull a client's TransUnion credit report in Forth.

The five main sections

Every report is organized into the same five areas: identifying information, public records, collections, trades (credit history), and inquiries. Optional add-ons like a credit summary or model/risk score may also appear at the top.

Public records & collections

Public records cover civil judgments, tax liens, and bankruptcies pulled from court records; retention on file ranges roughly from 7 years (civil judgments, paid tax liens, most bankruptcy dismissals) up to 10 years (unpaid tax liens, Chapter 7/11/12/13 bankruptcy filings). Collections show accounts that have been handed to a third-party collection agency, including the original creditor, amount placed, and current balance.

Trades (credit history)

Each trade line shows who the creditor is, when the account opened, the credit limit or original loan amount, current balance, and a payment history pattern going back up to 24 months. The MOP (Manner of Payment) code is the one to know at a glance:

MOPMeaning
01Pays as agreed
02–0530 / 60 / 90 / 120+ days past due
08 / 8ARepossession / voluntary repossession
09Charged off to bad debt
9BCollection account

Inquiries

Lists which companies have pulled the client's file over the last two years. A high number of recent inquiries is worth flagging — it can also trigger an ID-mismatch alert on the report itself.

Full reference This tab summarizes the TransUnion Credit Report User Guide. If you need the complete field-by-field breakdown or the full code tables (ECOA, KOB, date indicators), ask your team lead for the full PDF.

Final checklist before submitting

  • Confirmed whether the client is taking Level Coaching before selecting a base plan.
  • Base plan and document package match (LP with no coaching / non-LP + Purchase Agreement with coaching).
  • Program Length, Frequency, and payment setup confirmed — unchanged in both paths.
  • Cash flow is $250 or more after the program payment.
  • Banking info read back to the client before saving (unrecoverable after save).
  • Compliance script matches: "NO Benefits" unless coaching benefits are included.
  • Compliance email "To" field updated to contracts@level-debt.com before sending.
